clue.text: A learner joins class that's strict

parts.note: a form is a school class
L is the learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A new pupil enrols in a class run by a strict teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Something formal follows rules and conventions closely, so it is rigid or strict.

clue.text: Unfasten the duck cage

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O
a pen is an enclosure for animals, a cage

explanation.surface: Someone is told to unlock the cage where the duck is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a door or lid is to make it no longer shut, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Country professor on staff gets first-class write-up

indicators.note: on signals one piece attached to the other in sequence

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff of office
a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are written from the bottom, so they run backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, here read as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: A professor on the university staff gets a glowing review from back home.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is the old shipping-register mark for first-class, and 'write-up' reads it upward in this down entry. 'on' just joins the staff and the professor.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia is a Balkan nation, now officially North Macedonia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: General means to establish latitude

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a way is a means or method of doing something

explanation.surface: A commander uses some method to fix his position on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latitude' looks geographical, fitting General and establish, but it means freedom of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room for manoeuvre, the same idea as latitude meaning scope or freedom.

clue.text: Mortality figures are a total write-off

definitions.meaning: read literally, the tally of the dead in a disaster, those killed and lost

explanation.surface: Casualty statistics are dismissed by accountants as an unrecoverable sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead loss is an idiom for something completely useless, which is what a total write-off is.

clue.text: An exact report of the "Three Blind Mice"?

definitions.text: An exact report of the "Three Blind Mice"?

parts.words: An exact report of the "Three Blind Mice"?
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the mice's tails, so the story is literally one about losing tails; a thorough report means the same words

explanation.surface: A request for a precise record of the nursery rhyme about three blind mice.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so the tale is read as the mice being de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A full, thorough report giving every particular is the sense of an exact report.

clue.text: Go really wild with "Pilgrim's Progress", for example

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to have fun with Bunyan's classic book.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunyan's book is a famous symbolic story in which characters stand for virtues and vices, an example of the genre.

clue.text: A bulb may be a variety of tulip

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the flower's letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a bulb might turn out to be some kind of tulip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulb' suggests a flower bulb, matching tulip, but it is a light bulb, which may be switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bulb that is switched on is illuminated, which is the phrase's meaning.

clue.text: The points of savage attacks

parts.note: read literally, the sharp tips of weapons used by warriors; figuratively, the leading forces of assaults

explanation.surface: A note on what the sharp ends of weapons in a fierce assault are called.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tips of spears are their heads, and the term also means forces leading an attack.

clue.text: Everyone is absorbed in the trial case

indicators.note: being absorbed in something is being taken within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a test is a trial
each means every one taken individually

explanation.surface: Everybody is engrossed in the courtroom trial of the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' and 'trial' paint a court scene, but the case is a wooden packing box.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a light wooden box used for shipping tea and for packing, a type of case.

clue.text: Refuse a stretcher

definitions.meaning: the noun, rubbish or waste lying about
a frame for carrying a sick or injured person

explanation.surface: Someone declines to use a stretcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter means scattered rubbish and is also an old word for a carried bed or stretcher.

clue.text: Becoming less friendly, drag warpaint out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling hostile, someone hauls out the warpaint.
explanation.definitionFit: When people drift away from each other emotionally, their closeness weakens; a common idiom.

clue.text: One is apart, possibly result of marital trouble?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could form something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Being apart from a spouse may be what marriage problems lead to.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple's formal decision to live apart is a common outcome of an unhappy marriage.

clue.text: Sappers in control of cavalry?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers take command of the mounted troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavalry' suggests soldiers, but the control is a strap held by a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is the strap a rider uses to guide a horse, so it controls a mount.

clue.text: Setting for clips or decorations on a nobleman

indicators.note: on signals the decorations placed after the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
OBEs are British honours, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A nobleman wearing his medals has either clips or decorations pinned on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clips' are clip-on earrings, worn where the definition says.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip-on earrings are fixed to the soft lower part of the ear, so it is their mount.

clue.text: As ordered, one goes in the artillery

indicators.note: going in means being inserted into another piece

parts.note: ordnance means military weapons, especially artillery
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Following orders, a soldier joins the artillery regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official decree, so what it lays down is ordered by authority.

clue.text: Swindle companies and acknowledges it

parts.note: a con is a swindle
firms are businesses, companies

explanation.surface: A fraudster cheats businesses and openly admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm something is to state that it is true, which is to acknowledge it.

clue.text: One may feel wrongly persecuted because of it

definitions.text: One may feel wrongly persecuted because of it

parts.words: One may feel wrongly persecuted because of it
parts.note: describes a mental condition that makes a person believe falsely that others are plotting against them

explanation.surface: A description of a cause of feeling unfairly victimised.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition is marked by irrational suspicion and a belief that one is being targeted by others.

clue.text: Double act no longer seen

indicators.note: double means the following word is given twice

parts.note: do means act, to perform

explanation.surface: A comedy duo that has dropped out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double act' reads as a comic pair, but splits into an indicator and a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius died out centuries ago, so it is extinct and never seen now.

clue.text: One may be prone to use this, following inflation

definitions.text: One may be prone to use this, following inflation

parts.words: One may be prone to use this, following inflation
parts.note: prone means lying face down, and the item is blown up before use, rather than inflation in the economic sense

explanation.surface: Someone may become likely to do something after prices rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' reads as 'inclined' and 'inflation' as rising prices; both are literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable mattress is lain upon once blown up, exactly what the clue describes.

clue.text: A challenging demand

parts.note: a demand made when issuing a challenge, as when a gentleman insulted called for a duel

explanation.surface: A tough request that is hard to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: An insulted gentleman would 'demand satisfaction', challenging the other to a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, redress for an insult through a duel was what the challenger demanded.

clue.text: Scoring shot in billiards or from batting cricket side

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
the off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat

explanation.surface: A question about a scoring stroke in billiards or one made batting in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a stroke that pots a ball off another ball scores points, and that is its name.

clue.text: Tread the stage

definitions.meaning: the flat part of a stair that the foot rests on
one phase or point in a process

explanation.surface: An actor is told to walk onto the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair's footing surface and a phase in a process both share this word.

clue.text: A port, half an hour later, shows potency

indicators.note: later signals the second piece coming after the first

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

indicators.note: half takes one of the two halves of the word, here its back half

explanation.surface: Fortified wine taken half an hour later shows its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A port' suggests the drink, but it is the Spanish harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is strength and energy, which is what potency means.

clue.text: Courtesy of the townsman

definitions.meaning: the quality belonging to a city dweller, the urban type

explanation.surface: A gracious gesture from a city resident.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means suave politeness and literally the quality of the city-bred.

clue.text: Extinguishes a candle flame and passes on

definitions.meaning: puts out a flame by pinching it, with the candle as the object

explanation.surface: Someone puts out a candle and then hands something along.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase for dying literally describes snuffing out a flame, an apt image of life ending.

clue.text: Port required to finish university course

parts.note: to die is to come to an end, to finish
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a degree course at British universities such as Oxford

explanation.surface: Something is needed to complete a degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French ferry harbour on the Channel coast, an example of a port.
